To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the GAPDH gene of the extremely thermophillic archaebacter Methanothermus fervida is expressed in Escherichia coli cells and that the enzyme produced is thermostable and identical to the original protein from the archaebacter.
the glyceraldehyde 3‐phosphate (G3P) dehydrogenase of Methanothermus fervids has been cloned and expressed in E.coli, and that the recombinant enzyme was purified to homogeneity and characterized.
The gene of glyceraldhyde‐3‐phosphat‐dehydrogenase (EC 1.2.1.12) from the archaebacter Methanothermus fervidis has been cloned and expressed in Escherichia coli cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of an archaebacterial GAPDH gene in a mesophilic host and with the production of large amounts of a thermostable enzyme for X‐ray structure analysis.
the expression of an extremely thermophilic protein in a mesophilic host.
the expression of genes from archaebacteria in E. coli and the use of the E. Coli‐produced proteins for structural analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gene of the GAPDH from M. fervids was expressed in E. colli cells.
the GAPDH from M. fervi­ dus is a suitable enzyme for protein crystallization and X‐ray analysis, which can be easily produced in E. coli in high amounts.

the GAPDH from M. fervids is the first archaebacterial enzyme which has been cloned, expressed, and crystallized in E. coli, and which has been characterized with respect to its molecular properties and its thermostability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression system E. coli/pJF118EH allows the production of active proteins from thermophilic archæobacteria in a simple and rapid procedure.
the expression of a gene from an extremely thermophilic organism in E. coli can lead to the production of a protein that is identical in its properties to the protein synthesized by the archaebacter.
the GAPDH of the extremely thermophillic archaebacter M. fervidis is expressed in E. colicells and that the enzyme is suitable for protein crystallography.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GAPDH from M. fervids is an excellent model protein to study the molecular basis of thermostability.
the expression of a gene from an extreme thermophile in a mesophile such as E. coli is possible, and that the resulting enzyme is indistinguishable from the native enzyme.
the archaebacterial GAPDH is not a typical member of the GAPDH superfamily, but rather a novel member.
